summary: Tenant-aware graceful-degradation and rollback orchestration request for aggressive optimizer profile
description:
Issue summary:
BrightMed reports that after enabling an aggressive combined optimizer profile (async batching + kv-prefetch + mixed quant profile) for a subset of tenants on Dedicated capacity, a subset of their production traffic experienced elevated 95/99p latency and intermittent 5xxs. The customer wants guidance and an orchestrated safe rollback for the tenant to avoid global impact while reverting optimization flags.

Impact:
- Production request 95p latency increased from ~120ms to ~480ms for user-facing inference routes for ~10% of tokens.
- Error rate rose to 0.8% 5xx for that tenant's routes (previously ~0.02%).
- Customer-facing ML product degraded for BrightMed paying customers (dedicated pool).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (prod-us-east) serving pinned model rw-open-7b-v2 with tenant-specific optimizer overrides.
- Customer traffic routed through regional gateway -> dedicated GPU pool.

Steps to reproduce (observed in prod live traffic):
1) Tenant profile had optimizer flags enabled at 03:00 UTC (async-batching=true, kv-prefetch=enabled, quant-profile=qmixed-high).
2) Traffic slowly shifted from warm to steady-state volume over 20 minutes.
3) At 03:25 UTC, latency SLO breach alerts triggered and customer support received user reports.

Observed behavior:
- Sustained tail latency spike and transient memory pressure observed on several worker pods.
- Autoscaler attempted additional workers but allocation was delayed due to GPU availability constraints in dedicated pool.
- Rolling revert of optimizer flags at tenant scope was attempted manually but some routing rules applied globally, causing partial revert and inconsistent behavior.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-scoped rollback should atomically demote optimizer flags for only BrightMed traffic, preserving other tenants and not requiring global pool changes.

Temporary workaround performed by customer support prior to ticket creation:
- Scoped traffic split to route BrightMed traffic to a warm standby variant with conservative optimizer profile. This reduced 95p latency to ~160ms but increased cost.

Request:
- Guidance for orchestrated, tenant-scoped safe rollback of optimizer flags (batching, kv-prefetch, quant profiles) with minimal impact to other tenants and without forcing global pool redeploy.
- A short playbook runbook for the customer success engineer to perform an emergency rollback if automated rollback fails.

Additional constraints from customer:
- Cannot accept prolonged global pool degrading actions. Must keep impact contained to their tenant only.
- BrightMed requires post-mortem evidence for audit (timestamps, config deltas, traffic snapshots).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - BrightMed (Customer): We enabled the optimizer bundle from our CSE yesterday morning. After a brief improvement, tail latency jumped and some user requests timed out. We rolled back some flags but saw inconsistent routing — asking Redwood for a safe tenant-only rollback and steps we can run ourselves.

2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Maya Singh (Support): Acknowledged. Opening ticket and looping in SRE + Serving runtime so we can validate telemetry and provide an orchestrated rollback plan. First response target set per SLA.

2026-03-10 11:03 UTC - Luis Ortega (SRE): Collected pod-level metrics and stack traces. Observed evictions and increased GC cycles on workers with kv-prefetch enabled. Adding serving team to investigate kernel selection path and memory accounting.

2026-03-11 16:20 UTC - Claire Huang (Serving Eng): Hypothesis - combined async batching + prefetch with high quant compression increases transient memory fragmentation under mixed sequence length loads. Preparing a conservative rollback checklist that demotes features one-by-one with traffic guards.

2026-03-13 08:56 UTC - Luis Ortega (SRE): Customer accepted temporary traffic split. Requesting permission to run tenant-scoped config revert during low-traffic window (03:00-04:30 UTC) and to collect before/after traces for postmortem.
2026-03-14 12:05 UTC - BrightMed (Customer): Approved the proposed low-traffic window and asked for a short runbook they can follow if automatic revert fails.
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:30 UTC - Telemetry: 95p latency delta correlates with worker pods that had optimizer bundle applied and increased allocator churn.
03/10 10:00 UTC - Traces: Token generation spans show bursts of KV cache misses immediately after enablement, causing additional model steps and memory hot paths.
03/11 11:15 UTC - Autoscaler log: Pending scale-out events delayed by 120s due to reserved GPU pool saturation for dedicated customers in us-east.
03/12 14:40 UTC - Heap profiles: Elevated pinned allocations in serving runtime when mixed-quant profile used with prefetch enabled.

03/13 09:00 UTC - Reconciliation test on staging: Demoting kv-prefetch alone returned tail latency near baseline; demoting async-batching next provided additional stability. Quant profile demotion reduced memory pressure but increased per-token cost.
Recommended rollback order: 1) Disable tenant kv-prefetch, 2) Switch quant-profile to qbalanced, 3) Turn off async-batching aggressive mode, 4) Re-evaluate batching window and prewarm caches.
next_steps: Prepare tenant-scoped config snapshot and backup current optimizer flags for BrightMed (done).
Schedule controlled rollback during agreed low-traffic window 2026-03-15 03:00-04:30 UTC with customer on-call present.
Execute rollback in the recommended order with verification gates after each step (perf dashboard checks + 10-minute stabilization).
If rollback step fails to improve metrics, immediately revert that step and escalate to Serving Eng for live investigation.
Produce postmortem with collected traces, config deltas, and timeline within 72 hours of completion.
